request.query: What changed in the UPI Lite limits addendum compared with the baseline? Include source-backed conditions and dates, and identify unresolved points.

claims.text: The 2025 addendum (Circular 169A) increases the per-transaction limit from ₹500 to ₹1,000 and raises the total account limit from ₹2,000 to ₹5,000, whereas the 2023 baseline (Circular 169) set the per-transaction limit at ₹500 with a total limit of ₹2,000. The 2025 addendum also introduces new conditions regarding online-mode replenishment and auto top-up options absent in the 2023 circular.

quotes.quote: NPCI/UPI/OC No. 169 A/2024-25 — 27th February 2025 To, All UPI Members Dear Sir/Madam, **Subject: Addendum to Enhancement in UPI LITE Limits** With reference to the NPCI/UPI/OC No. 138/2021-22, dated 16th March 2022 and NPCI/UPI/OC No. 169/2023-24, dated 31st August 2023, UPI LITE was introduced and transaction limit was increased from ₹200 from ₹500 respectively. > Transcription note: the source itself uses “from ₹200 from ₹500”; that wording is retained.

NPCI/UPI/OC No. 169/2023-24 31st August 2023 To All Member-Unified Payments Interface (UPI) Dear Madam/Sir, **Subject: Enhancement in UPI LITE transaction limit to ₹500** UPI LITE has been designed to play a vital role in reducing infrastructure load on the Core Banking System of the banks. This feature has been making the small value transactions faster and highly reliable for transaction value below ₹200. As per the latest circular issued by RBI on 24th August, 2023 vide Circular No: RBI/2023-24/57 CO.DPSS.POLC.No.S526/02-14-003/2023-24 with subject ‘Enhancing transaction limits for Small Value Digital Payments in Offline Mode’, the upper limit of an offline payment transaction is now increased from ₹200 to ₹500. In view of the above, the per transaction value limit for UPI LITE (Purpose code 44 - Online and 45 - Offline) has now been enhanced to ₹500. The details are as below: | UPI LITE Limit | Previous Limit | New Limit | |---|---|---| | Per Transaction | ₹200 | ₹500 | | Max balance in UPI lite account | ₹2000 | ₹2000 (No change) | The existing UPI pricing shall be applicable for transaction amount ₹201-₹500 for both P2P and P2M transactions. With reference to the above, Member Banks (Payee PSP), Third Party App providers (TPAPs), Merchants and other payment providers are requested to take note of the above enhancement

1. As per the latest notification issued by RBI on 4th December 2024 vide circular no. RBI/2021-22/146 CO.DPSS.POLC.No.S1264/02-14-003/2021-2022 with subject ‘Framework for Facilitating Small Value Digital Payments in Offline Mode’, for UPI LITE, the enhanced limits shall be ₹1,000 per transaction with ₹5,000 being the total limit. Replenishment of used limit shall be allowed only in online mode with AFA. Customer will further have the option to set Auto Top-up for limit replenishment as per NPCI circular, ‘Introduction of Auto Top-up on UPI LITE’, vide No. NPCI/UPI/OC No. 205/2024-25, dated 27th August 2024. The details of the LITE limits are as below: | Description | UPI LITE — Existing | UPI LITE — New | UPI LITE X (Offline) — No Change | |---|---|---|---| | Per Transaction Limit | ₹500 | ₹1000 | ₹500 | | Total Limit at any point in time | ₹2000 | ₹5000 | ₹2000 | The new limits shall apply to and govern all existing NPCI circulars pertaining to UPI LITE limit (Annexure A). All the members are required to make the necessary changes pertaining to limit increase immediately.

findings.reason: The answer claims the addendum raises the total account limit from ₹2,000 to ₹5,000. However, excerpt S2.2 (baseline) explicitly states the 'Max balance in UPI lite account' remains at ₹2,000 with '(No change)', while excerpt S5.1 (addendum) shows a table where the 'Total Limit at any point in time' for 'UPI LITE — New' is listed as ₹5,000 but the column header structure and context of S5.1 suggest this might be conflating different limit types or misinterpreting the table which lists 'Per Transaction Limit' as ₹1000 and 'Total Limit' as ₹5000 for a specific category (UPI LITE X - Offline) while keeping others at ₹2000. The answer simplifies this into a direct increase without clarifying if the ₹5,000 applies universally or to a specific new category, creating ambiguity about whether the baseline limit of ₹2,000 is fully superseded or if it coexists.

quotes.quote: NPCI/UPI/OC No. 169 A/2024-25 — 27th February 2025 To, All UPI Members Dear Sir/Madam, **Subject: Addendum to Enhancement in UPI LITE Limits** With reference to the NPCI/UPI/OC No. 138/2021-22, dated 16th March 2022 and NPCI/UPI/OC No. 169/2023-24, dated 31st August 2023, UPI LITE was introduced and transaction limit was increased from ₹200 from ₹500 respectively. > Transcription note: the source itself uses “from ₹200 from ₹500”; that wording is retained.

NPCI/UPI/OC No. 169/2023-24 31st August 2023 To All Member-Unified Payments Interface (UPI) Dear Madam/Sir, **Subject: Enhancement in UPI LITE transaction limit to ₹500** UPI LITE has been designed to play a vital role in reducing infrastructure load on the Core Banking System of the banks. This feature has been making the small value transactions faster and highly reliable for transaction value below ₹200. As per the latest circular issued by RBI on 24th August, 2023 vide Circular No: RBI/2023-24/57 CO.DPSS.POLC.No.S526/02-14-003/2023-24 with subject ‘Enhancing transaction limits for Small Value Digital Payments in Offline Mode’, the upper limit of an offline payment transaction is now increased from ₹200 to ₹500. In view of the above, the per transaction value limit for UPI LITE (Purpose code 44 - Online and 45 - Offline) has now been enhanced to ₹500. The details are as below: | UPI LITE Limit | Previous Limit | New Limit | |---|---|---| | Per Transaction | ₹200 | ₹500 | | Max balance in UPI lite account | ₹2000 | ₹2000 (No change) | The existing UPI pricing shall be applicable for transaction amount ₹201-₹500 for both P2P and P2M transactions. With reference to the above, Member Banks (Payee PSP), Third Party App providers (TPAPs), Merchants and other payment providers are requested to take note of the above enhancement

1. As per the latest notification issued by RBI on 4th December 2024 vide circular no. RBI/2021-22/146 CO.DPSS.POLC.No.S1264/02-14-003/2021-2022 with subject ‘Framework for Facilitating Small Value Digital Payments in Offline Mode’, for UPI LITE, the enhanced limits shall be ₹1,000 per transaction with ₹5,000 being the total limit. Replenishment of used limit shall be allowed only in online mode with AFA. Customer will further have the option to set Auto Top-up for limit replenishment as per NPCI circular, ‘Introduction of Auto Top-up on UPI LITE’, vide No. NPCI/UPI/OC No. 205/2024-25, dated 27th August 2024. The details of the LITE limits are as below: | Description | UPI LITE — Existing | UPI LITE — New | UPI LITE X (Offline) — No Change | |---|---|---|---| | Per Transaction Limit | ₹500 | ₹1000 | ₹500 | | Total Limit at any point in time | ₹2000 | ₹5000 | ₹2000 | The new limits shall apply to and govern all existing NPCI circulars pertaining to UPI LITE limit (Annexure A). All the members are required to make the necessary changes pertaining to limit increase immediately.
